# ARIA Architecture

## System Overview

ARIA is a modular Python terminal assistant for Termux/Android, with a Rich REPL, remote model providers, an offline knowledge base and a local repair planner. This description was checked against the supplied source on 2026-11-14; no runtime, device or network checks were performed.

Start with [project context](CONTEXT.md) for current state and unresolved work. [README](README.md) owns user setup and commands; [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md) owns development procedures. Source paths below identify evidence in the full project; the Markdown-only handoff does not include those files.

## Component Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    ENTRY["run_aria.py or aria.main:main"] --> REPL["ARIA / main.py"]
    REPL --> CONFIG["ConfigManager"]
    REPL --> CMD["CommandSystem"]
    CMD --> HANDLERS["ARIA command handlers"]
    HANDLERS --> API["APIClient"]
    API --> GOOGLE["Google SDK or REST"]
    API --> COMPAT["OpenRouter / NVIDIA NIM"]
    HANDLERS --> KB["KnowledgeBase"]
    HANDLERS --> REPAIR["RepairAgent"]
    REPAIR --> GUARDIAN["Guardian analysis for local auto-repair"]
    REPAIR --> SUBPROCESS["Subprocess execution"]
    REPL --> WATCH["WatchMode polling thread"]
    FILES["Shell hook / log files / tracked PIDs"] --> WATCH
    WATCH --> QUEUE["Pending notifications"]
    QUEUE --> REPL
    REPL --> UI["UIManager / Rich"]
```

Evidence: `setup.py` entry points, `run_aria.py`, `aria/main.py` construction, registration and run loop. There is no `aria/cli.py` in this snapshot and no Click dependency. This is one application with a command worker and a watcher thread, not evidence of an autonomous multi-agent scheduler.

## Data Flow

### Command Execution Flow

```text
Launch → load config → setup wizard if required → initialize API client
       → register slash handlers → optional watcher → REPL
User input
  ├─ /exit, /quit, exit, quit → stop
  ├─ recognized slash command → handler
  │    ├─ /ask → provider → display text
  │    ├─ /fix → failure context → local plan, otherwise provider diagnosis
  │    ├─ /install → install plan → confirmation or auto_apply → execute
  │    ├─ /kb → local knowledge lookup
  │    ├─ /watch → toggle or manage targets
  │    └─ /config, /provider, /model → configuration operations
  └─ unrecognized input (including unknown slash commands) → /ask
```

`CommandSystem.parse_command` trims text, removes the slash and splits once on whitespace; it is not a shell parser. Arguments remain strings. Registration supports aliases, but the main registry supplies none; `/models` is registered separately. History is an in-memory list.

`ARIA.run` dispatches handlers through `_execute_with_timeout` using a single-worker executor and a 90-second future wait. This is not a proven hard cancellation: executor context exit waits for running work. `CommandSystem.execute` retries a handler without `status_handler` on any `TypeError`, including one raised inside the handler.

`cmd_ask` and model-assisted `cmd_fix` strip `<thought>` blocks before returning text. Model suggestions are displayed, not automatically executed by these handlers. `UIManager.display_response` also attempts to copy the first command from a fenced code block to the Termux clipboard.

### Error Detection & Fix Flow

```text
Shell failure → installed shell hook → ~/.aria/last_fail.json
Log output → watch.log, runtime_errors.log, or a registered target log
                         ↓
WatchMode polls about once per second → queues events
                         ↓
REPL checks queue before its next input prompt → notification
                         ↓
User invokes /fix → reads hook (then clears it), else watch.log tail
                 → adds explicit error text; bash history is last resort
                 → local repair plan
                    ├─ matched + auto_apply false → display plan
                    ├─ matched + auto_apply true → eligible local steps
                    └─ no local match → provider diagnosis if context exists
```

Evidence: `aria/watch_mode.py` lifecycle, polling and notification methods; `aria/main.py:cmd_fix`; `install.sh` hook definitions. Watch detection does not itself invoke repairs. Notifications wait for the REPL to return to its prompt boundary.

The hook is a single latest-failure slot, not a queue. The Bash installer hook writes `cmd`, `code`, `cwd`, `ts`; neither installer hook captures stderr. The Zsh hook omits `ts`, while `WatchMode._check_hook_file` requires a new nonempty timestamp. Manual `/fix` reads the JSON without that timestamp requirement.

Watch targets are stored as `{"targets": [...]}`; supported fields include `id`, `pid`, `log`, `name`, `oneshot`. PID liveness uses signal 0. A process-exit event reports disappearance, not the process exit code. `/watch add` splits fields on whitespace, so paths/names with spaces are not handled as quoted arguments. On enable, existing logs are positioned at EOF and the current hook timestamp is remembered. Notifications for target logs and runtime errors do not feed their event context into `cmd_fix`, which reads only the hook, `watch.log`, explicit text or history.

### API Self-Healing Flow

```text
generate_content → validate model against fetched/cached list
  ├─ list unavailable → permit attempted generation with configured model
  └─ configured model absent from nonempty list → select first available
       ↓
Generate (default: at most 3 attempts)
  ├─ success → text
  ├─ nonretryable error → stop
  └─ retryable error → wait 1s then 2s between attempts
       ↓
Exhaustion → error text suggesting /kb and provider/config commands
```

Evidence: `aria/api_client.py:APIClient`. Fallback is an error/help string, not offline model inference. An automatic model change in `generate_content` changes the client's in-memory config; it does not save the JSON file.

## Module Responsibilities

All module names below are relative to `aria/`, except the launcher.

| Module | Responsibility | Key features |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main.py` | Application composition and REPL | Setup, slash handlers, provider switching, failure context |
| `run_aria.py` (root) | Standalone launch | Imports ARIA and calls `run` |
| `api_client.py` | Provider abstraction | Google SDK/REST, OpenAI-compatible providers, retries, key checks |
| `command_system.py` | Dispatch | Registration, parsing, aliases and in-memory history |
| `config.py` | JSON configuration | Default backfill, environment overrides, save/reset |
| `guardian.py` | Risk classification | Regex analysis and confirmation flag; does not itself prompt |
| `knowledge_base.py` | Offline troubleshooting | Embedded entries, substring and fuzzy lookup |
| `repair_agent.py` | Local plans and execution | Package mappings, bounded auto-repair, install plans |
| `watch_mode.py` | Background observation | Hook/log polling, target PIDs, queued notifications, legacy fix helper |
| `ui.py` | Terminal display/input | Rich formatting, status indicators, clipboard and system-info helpers |
| `utils.py` | Utilities | Termux detection, shell-command helper, formatting |

## Configuration Architecture

```text
~/.aria/
├── config.json          # Config and API keys, plain JSON
├── aria.log             # Application log (plain FileHandler)
├── last_fail.json        # Latest shell-hook failure
├── watch.log            # User-directed command output
├── runtime_errors.log   # Additional watched log
└── watch_targets.json   # Registered PID/log targets
```

These are application paths, not personal workspace details. `main.py` creates the log directory and replaces root logging handlers at import time. No log rotation is configured there.

### Configuration Schema

See the [README example](README.md#config). `ConfigManager.DEFAULT_CONFIG` starts with empty `provider`, `model`, `api_key`, an empty `api_keys` map, `temperature=0.7`, `max_tokens=8192`, `guardian_mode=true`, and `watch_mode=auto_apply=false`. It also has `created_at` and `updated_at` (initially null). Save sets `updated_at`; reset sets `created_at`. The wizard can add `_key_validated`.

Load order in `config.py`: file or defaults → migration/backfill → general `ARIA_*` variables → provider-specific keys. `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `NVIDIA_NIM_API_KEY` populate `api_keys` and replace the active key when the provider matches. At startup, `ARIA.setup` prefers `api_keys[provider]` over the general `api_key`; a saved provider key can therefore supersede `ARIA_API_KEY`.

`ConfigManager.validate` checks only for a key, not a model, provider validity or live authentication. The REPL setup requires nonempty provider/model/key and may run the wizard. A failed live key check warns but does not necessarily prevent startup. See [open issues](CONTEXT.md#open-issues-and-proposed-next-actions) for configuration synchronization gaps.

## Knowledge Base Structure

`KnowledgeBase._load_entries` defines 28 entries in this snapshot:

```text
Knowledge Base
├── errors (11): command_not_found, permission_denied, compiler/tool errors
├── package_management (4): update, search, clean, mirror
├── proot (3): install, login, backup
├── android_bridge (6): battery, clipboard, notification, share, camera, speech
└── development (4): venv, Git config, SSH key, port forwarding
```

Search checks query substring in pattern, then solution, then `difflib.SequenceMatcher` against pattern (default threshold 0.6). Results follow insertion order; they are not sorted by similarity. Local repair requests a 0.75 threshold. Entries carry `pattern`, `solution`, `auto_fixable`, optional `fix_command`, and `category`. These are troubleshooting suggestions, not device-tested guarantees. The older 100+ claim remains only as historical changelog text.

## Command Registration System

This illustrates the registration API; `q` and `query` are example aliases, not currently registered commands:

```python
command_system.register(
    name="ask",
    handler=cmd_ask,
    description="Ask the AI a question",
    aliases=["q", "query"],
    requires_args=True
)
parsed = command_system.parse_command("/ask How to install Python?")
result = command_system.execute(parsed)
```

## API Integration

| Provider | Transport and base URL | Authentication |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Google | Installed `google.generativeai` SDK; otherwise `urllib` REST at `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta` | REST uses `x-goog-api-key` header |
| OpenRouter | `urllib`, `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | Bearer key; HTTP-Referer and X-Title headers |
| NVIDIA NIM | `urllib`, `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1` | Bearer key |

Evidence: `aria/api_client.py`. OpenAI-compatible providers use `GET /models` and non-streaming `POST /chat/completions`. Google REST lists up to ten pages, filters for `generateContent` support when methods are supplied, and posts to `/models/{model}:generateContent`. A model that rejects a separate system instruction can receive one retry with the instruction folded into the prompt. Response extraction omits thought parts and reports blocked/empty responses.

Google key validation lists models. OpenAI-compatible key validation sends a one-token completion because a public models endpoint would not establish authentication. The validation helper accepts some error messages containing `404`, `not found` or `unavailable`; its success message alone does not prove usable inference. Live model availability, provider quotas and pricing were not checked. Historical free-tier numbers are not current guarantees.

### Self-Healing Mechanism

See [API flow](#api-self-healing-flow) for model selection and retry limits. SDK preference and REST fallback are implementation choices. The [changelog](CHANGELOG.md#unreleased) records the rationale: SDK installation problems on Termux, fewer dependencies, and non-streaming reliability on mobile connections.

## Guardian Safety Layer

### Risk Scoring Algorithm

`Guardian.analyze_command` checks safe regex patterns first using unanchored `re.search`. Any safe match returns LOW immediately. Otherwise it selects the highest matching dangerous level; no match also returns LOW. Scores are fixed by level, not additive.

### Risk Levels

| Level | Score | Analyzer confirmation flag |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LOW | 0 | false |
| MEDIUM | 40 | true |
| HIGH | 70 | true |
| CRITICAL | 100 | true |

Examples of declared patterns: `rm -rf` is CRITICAL; `sudo` and `chmod 777` are HIGH; `eval` is MEDIUM. Pattern coverage is limited: safe substrings can mask dangerous parts, and the pipe-to-shell regex does not generally match a URL between `curl` and the pipe.

Execution paths differ:

- `RepairAgent.attempt_auto_repair` defaults to planning only. With `auto_apply`, it filters steps by `auto_run`, Guardian confirmation flag and allowed installation-command prefixes, runs at most four, and stops on a nonzero result. Failed-command parsing rejects shell metacharacters. Execution uses argument lists with a 900-second subprocess timeout.
- `/install` calls `execute_plan` after a UI confirmation unless `auto_apply` is enabled. This executor does not apply the local-repair prefix filter, Guardian gate or four-step cap. The UI confirmation defaults to yes, including its EOF/interrupt fallback.
- The legacy `WatchMode.execute_fix` and `utils.run_command` use `shell=True` without Guardian checks. They are not the normal watch notification flow.
- `plan_from_ai_text` can parse code blocks into steps, but the inspected `/ask` and `/fix` handlers do not call it.

Guardian is advisory logic, not a sandbox or universal authorization boundary. The app constructs Guardian enabled; setup only enables it conditionally and does not disable it when the saved preference is false. See [context](CONTEXT.md#open-issues-and-proposed-next-actions) for the proposed repair work.

## Testing Architecture

The supplied tests cover these areas by assertions, not by verified results from this review:

| Test module | Inspected coverage |
| --- | --- |
| `test_api_client.py` | Config/init/fallback; mocked REST selection, pagination/filtering, auth header, generation payload, instruction fallback, invalid/empty/blocked responses |
| `test_command_system.py` | Registration, parsing, handler execution, aliases, history |
| `test_config.py` | Custom config path, save/load, get/set, key presence, reset |
| `test_guardian.py` | Simple safe/dangerous examples, fixed scores, enabled/toggle, emoji |
| `test_knowledge_base.py` | Initialization, lookup, categories, loose fuzzy-search assertion |
| `test_repair_agent.py` | Missing command/module and cryptography plans; mocked subprocess execution |
| `test_watch_mode.py` | Thread lifecycle, hook/log detection, clearing notifications |

No supplied `test_main.py` or installer integration suite was listed. There is no retained coverage report in the supplied inventory. See [testing procedures](CONTRIBUTING.md#testing) for commands and the real-home filesystem caveat.

## Performance Characteristics

No benchmarks were supplied or run. Earlier startup/search/API timing estimates are not substantiated measurements. Source constants establish approximately one-second watcher polling, a default 60-second REST generation timeout, a 90-second future wait in the REPL, and a 900-second repair subprocess timeout. These are different limits; none establishes end-to-end latency.

## Scalability Considerations

The KB and registry are in-memory structures; configuration is JSON with unknown fields preserved by default merging. No measured entry/command capacity is established. Provider limits are external. Command history, notification queues and application logs have no demonstrated capacity/rotation guarantees in the inspected code.

## Security Considerations

API keys are saved in plain JSON; no explicit restrictive chmod is applied by `ConfigManager.save`. The key prompt uses ordinary console input, not password input. `ConfigManager.display` masks the top-level key only, leaving the nested `api_keys` map visible; avoid sharing raw config output.

Provider traffic uses HTTPS in the inspected endpoints. Model-assisted `/fix` may transmit failed commands, cwd, error/log excerpts or recent Bash history to the active provider. Keep secrets out of submitted context. Guardian has the limits above; parsing a slash command does not provide shell escaping or execution isolation.

## Extension Points

### Adding New Commands

```python
def cmd_custom(args: str) -> str:
    """Custom command handler."""
    return f"Custom response: {args}"

aria.command_system.register(
    name="custom",
    handler=cmd_custom,
    description="Custom command",
    requires_args=True
)
```

Register application handlers in `ARIA._register_commands`; handlers can accept `status_handler` for updates. Follow the [contribution guidelines](CONTRIBUTING.md).

### Adding Knowledge Base Entries

```python
kb.entries["custom_error"] = KBEntry(
    pattern="custom error pattern",
    solution="How to solve this error",
    auto_fixable=True,
    fix_command="fix command",
    category="custom"
)
```

This example mutates an instance. Durable bundled entries belong in `KnowledgeBase._load_entries`; review any auto-fix command independently.

### Custom API Integration

Implement `BaseProvider.list_models` and `generate`, or use `OpenAICompatProvider` for compatible endpoints. Register the provider in `APIClient.SUPPORTED_PROVIDERS` and `_initialize_provider`, then update wizard validation, key mapping and UI labels. Raise `ProviderError` with retryability appropriate to the failure. A client subclass alone does not wire a provider into the REPL.

## Deployment Architecture

```text
Full source checkout + dependencies
  ├─ python run_aria.py → ARIA.run
  └─ pip install -e . → console command aria → aria.main:main → ARIA.run
                           ↓
                    configuration/setup → interactive REPL
```

There are no implemented shell subcommands such as `aria ask`; use `/ask` inside the REPL. `install.sh` additionally changes shell startup files, removes prior ARIA hook blocks, adds hooks/PATH, and creates or adjusts config. Manual README installation does not install those hooks. The script's fallback launcher assumes a relative installation location; it is not verified for arbitrary checkout locations.

# Changelog

All notable changes to ARIA will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Multi-provider support: Google AI Studio, OpenRouter, and NVIDIA NIM (2026-05-21)
- Animated logo and a local-first auto-repair agent (`repair_agent.py`) (2026-05-21)
- API keys are validated on save with a real auth check, not just an endpoint ping (2026-05-28)

### Changed

- Google provider falls back to plain HTTPS (stdlib `urllib`) when `google-generativeai` isn't installed, so it works on Termux setups where the SDK won't install. The SDK is still used when present (2026-10-14)
- When a provider can't initialize, the reason is now reported instead of `None` (2026-10-14)
- Trimmed dependencies: `rich` is the only required package, and `google-generativeai` is optional (Google provider only) (2026-05-28)
- Config schema aligned between the installer and the runtime (2026-05-28)
- `install.sh` no longer hardcodes the wrong directory name (2026-05-28)
- README rewritten twice: direct tone (2026-05-28), then for the post-hackathon phase (2026-10-14)
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` and package metadata corrected to point at this repository (2026-10-14)

### Fixed

- Google provider was unusable without `google-generativeai`: `/model list` returned nothing and `/ask` failed ([#2](https://github.com/Alex72-py/aria-termux/issues/2)) (2026-10-14)
- Stuck spinner and text wrapping on small screens (2026-05-28)
- Blocking confirmation prompts removed from threaded commands (2026-05-28)

### Removed

- Streaming mode, because non-streaming is more reliable on mobile connections (2026-05-28)

## [1.0.0] - 2026-05-24

### Added

- **Core Application**
  - Main ARIA application with interactive CLI
  - Slash command system with dynamic command registration
  - Configuration management with JSON storage
  - Comprehensive logging system

- **API Integration**
  - Google AI Studio API client with self-healing capabilities
  - Automatic model detection and switching
  - Exponential backoff retry logic
  - Graceful fallback to offline mode
  - Support for multiple Gemma 4 models

- **Guardian Safety Layer**
  - Risk scoring algorithm (0-100)
  - Dangerous pattern detection
  - User confirmation prompts for high-risk operations
  - Configurable safety mode

- **Watch Mode**
  - Real-time shell output monitoring
  - Error pattern detection
  - Auto-fix command execution
  - Integration with knowledge base

- **Knowledge Base**
  - 100+ Termux-specific entries
  - Fuzzy search matching
  - Category-based organization
  - Error patterns, package management, proot-distro, Android bridge

- **Rich Terminal UI**
  - ASCII art boot sequence
  - Spinner animations (neural, scan, pulse)
  - Syntax highlighting for code blocks
  - Color-coded output (error, success, info, warning)
  - Table display for structured data
  - Progress indicators

- **Commands**
  - `/ask <query>` - Ask the AI a question
  - `/fix <error>` - Analyze and fix errors
  - `/watch` - Enable watch mode
  - `/models` - List available models
  - `/config` - Run configuration wizard
  - `/kb <query>` - Search knowledge base
  - `/history` - Show command history
  - `/help` - Display help menu
  - `/exit` - Exit ARIA

- **CLI Interface**
  - Interactive REPL mode
  - Command-line arguments support
  - Configuration wizard
  - Help system

- **Testing**
  - Comprehensive test suite (26 tests)
  - Tests for API client, command system, knowledge base, Guardian, and config
  - Pytest integration with coverage reporting

- **Documentation**
  - Comprehensive README with installation and usage
  - Contributing guidelines
  - Architecture documentation
  - Inline code documentation with docstrings
  - Examples and use cases

- **Project Setup**
  - Python package with setuptools
  - Requirements.txt with all dependencies
  - MIT License
  - .gitignore for version control

### Features

- **Self-Healing API**: Automatically detects wrong models, fetches available ones, and retries
- **Offline Mode**: Full offline functionality with embedded knowledge base
- **Zero Credit Card**: Works with Google AI Studio free tier (15 req/min, 1500 req/day)
- **Termux Native**: Deep knowledge of Termux constraints and best practices
- **Beautiful UI**: Cinematic boot sequence and rich terminal output
- **Safe Operations**: Guardian mode prevents dangerous commands

### Technical Details

- **Language**: Python 3.8+
- **Platform**: Termux/Android, Linux
- **API**: Google Generative AI (Gemma 4)
- **UI Framework**: Rich
- **CLI Framework**: Click
- **Testing**: Pytest

### Known Limitations

- Requires Google AI Studio API key (free tier available)
- Watch mode requires shell output monitoring capability
- Some Android versions may have permission restrictions
- API rate limits apply (free tier: 15 req/min, 1500 req/day)

## Roadmap

The planned-features list that used to live here was written during the hackathon and is out of date. Current work is tracked in [issues](https://github.com/Alex72-py/aria-termux/issues).

---

## How to Report Issues

Found a bug? Please open an issue on GitHub with:
- Description of the bug
- Steps to reproduce
- Expected vs actual behavior
- Environment details (Termux version, Android version, Python version)

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! Please see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidelines.

---

# ARIA project context

## Start here

ARIA (Autonomous Repair and Intelligence Agent) is a Python terminal co-pilot for Termux/Android. It answers questions through remote models, searches embedded troubleshooting knowledge, monitors local failure files and plans or applies selected package repairs. Linux is mentioned as a secondary platform; no platform was tested in this review.

This is the returning-collaborator entry point, based on static inspection of the supplied project on **2026-11-14**. No project code, tests, installers, builds or network requests were executed. A Markdown-only recipient receives the documentation and root LICENSE, not source, configuration, tests, dot-paths or installed skills. The source locations cited below are provenance for a future full checkout; the useful findings are retained here and in the linked Markdown.

Read in this order:

1. This file: current state, limits and unresolved work.
2. [README](README.md): user-facing installation, configuration and command reference.
3. [ARCHITECTURE](ARCHITECTURE.md): source-backed flows, execution boundaries and module map.
4. [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md): development workflow, test procedures and the test-home caveat.
5. [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md): historical changes and rationale, not proof of current test results.
6. [AGENTS](AGENTS.md): ongoing context-maintenance guidance and its setup status.

## Current state

The [README status](README.md#status) says the hackathon phase has ended and work is driven by issues and pull requests, with one maintainer. It describes the core features as stable. The [changelog roadmap](CHANGELOG.md#roadmap) explicitly retires the older hackathon feature list in favor of GitHub issues. Those external issues were not accessed; active assignments, priorities and release timing are unknown.

Package metadata in `setup.py` and `aria/__init__.py` says **1.0.0**; `setup.py` also classifies development status as Beta and declares Python >=3.8. Internal “v4”/“v4.1” comments in main/watch/installer code are implementation labels, not evidence of a published 4.x release. Compatibility with the declared Python floor is unverified.

The latest dated entries in [Unreleased](CHANGELOG.md#unreleased) are 2026-10-14. They record Google REST fallback when the SDK cannot install, better initialization error reporting, and documentation/metadata corrections. Source and mocked regression tests support the presence of the REST implementation; they do not establish live availability or a published release.

### Supported progress view

Project direction: maintain a practical Termux assistant after the challenge, through issues and PRs [G].

```text
Termux assistant [G]
├─ PRESENT IN SOURCE: REPL + three providers + offline KB [A]
├─ PRESENT IN SOURCE: watch notifications + local repair planning [A]
│  └─ OPEN: hook, execution and configuration gaps [B]
└─ UNVERIFIED: runtime/device compatibility, test pass state, live providers [C]

PROPOSED NEXT: reproduce the highest-impact execution/configuration gaps
              in a disposable environment, then agree a scoped fix [B, C].
```

[G] [Project status](README.md#status) and [roadmap](CHANGELOG.md#roadmap).
[A] [Component and data flows](ARCHITECTURE.md#component-architecture).
[B] [Open issues below](#open-issues-and-proposed-next-actions).
[C] [Testing procedures and evidence limits](CONTRIBUTING.md#testing).

“Present” means inspected code exists, not that a feature passed validation. Proposed checks are documentation-review recommendations, not an approved product roadmap or an assigned work queue.

## Working model

| Area | What the supplied source establishes | Canonical detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Launch | `python run_aria.py` or installed `aria` enters `ARIA.run`; no Click CLI or shell subcommands | [Deployment flow](ARCHITECTURE.md#deployment-architecture) |
| Dependencies | `rich>=13.0.0` is the sole required dependency; Google SDK is an optional extra | [README dependencies](README.md#dependencies) |
| Providers | Google chooses installed SDK or stdlib REST; OpenRouter/NVIDIA use stdlib OpenAI-compatible HTTP | [API integration](ARCHITECTURE.md#api-integration) |
| Model requests | Non-streaming; bounded retries and model-list fallback; failure returns error text pointing to offline help | [API flow](ARCHITECTURE.md#api-self-healing-flow) |
| Offline help | Embedded KB search makes no model request; REPL setup still requires provider/model/key fields | [KB structure](ARCHITECTURE.md#knowledge-base-structure) |
| Repairs | Local planning first; default `auto_apply=false`; install execution has a different gate from local auto-repair | [Guardian and execution](ARCHITECTURE.md#guardian-safety-layer) |
| Watch | Polling thread queues hook/log/PID events; UI drains them before the next prompt | [Error detection](ARCHITECTURE.md#error-detection--fix-flow) |
| Persistence | JSON config and runtime files under `~/.aria`; in-memory command history; plain application log | [Config architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-architecture) |

## Decisions, rationale and boundaries

The existing contributor guidance asks for simple code, minimal new dependencies, PEP 8 and tests for new features. Its >80% coverage target is not a measured baseline. Existing PR guidelines ask for maintainer review; this documentation task did not authorize code changes, commits, pushes or releases.

The [changelog](CHANGELOG.md#unreleased) records two useful rationales: non-streaming was retained for mobile reliability, and Google REST fallback avoids a dependency that can be hard to install on Termux. Preserve these constraints when proposing provider changes. No ADR or explicit approval record for new design changes was supplied.

Earlier architecture claims about Click, 100+ KB entries, additive risk scores, universal Guardian protection, log rotation and performance timings conflicted with the inspected code or lacked evidence. The current [architecture guide](ARCHITECTURE.md) corrects them. The changelog's historical 1.0.0 descriptions, counts, quota numbers and safety wording remain preserved as history; they should not be copied as current guarantees.

The handoff uses visible root Markdown alongside the existing documents. This is an adoption layout choice for portability, not an inferred owner decision to migrate private notes or enable logging. No Context Docs event journal was enabled.

## Open issues and proposed next actions

These findings come from static reading. Source files were not changed, defects were not reproduced, and external issue ownership is unknown. Proposed checks below define a useful stopping condition without assigning a release obligation.

| Finding | Evidence and implication | Proposed next check / completion condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Execution gates differ and Guardian is incomplete | `guardian.py:analyze_command` returns LOW for any safe substring before checking dangerous patterns. `repair_agent.py:execute_plan` bypasses the filter used by `attempt_auto_repair`; legacy shell helpers have no Guardian gate. `ui.py:confirm` defaults to yes on EOF/interrupt. | With mocked executors, verify mixed-command classification and install/repair confirmation behavior; agree a consistent policy before changing code. Details: [execution boundaries](ARCHITECTURE.md#guardian-safety-layer). |
| `/fix --apply` is not an implemented flag | `main.py:cmd_fix` appends this hint but treats the entire argument as error text. Execution depends on saved `auto_apply`. | Add a handler-level regression demonstrating the chosen explicit-apply behavior, or remove the hint; do not assume the displayed instruction works. |
| Saved config and active objects diverge | `cmd_config` runs the wizard without rebuilding the client/Guardian; `_set_provider_key` saves without reloading. Setup never disables the initially enabled Guardian when preference is false. Model fallback during reload can save a model different from the already-created client's model. | Test setup, key/provider/model changes and status against the actual client and Guardian; completion means saved values and active behavior agree after each supported change. See [config load order](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-schema). |
| Hook and watch integration gaps | The installer Zsh hook omits `ts`; watcher requires it. Installer hooks supply no stderr. Runtime/target-log notifications suggest `/fix`, but `cmd_fix` does not consume their queued context. | Verify Bash/Zsh event payloads and a target-log failure with file fixtures; completion means the notified error reaches diagnosis and each supported hook is detected. [Watch flow](ARCHITECTURE.md#error-detection--fix-flow). |
| REPL timeout is not a hard stop | `main.py:_execute_with_timeout` waits on a future inside an executor context that waits for workers at exit. Repair subprocesses permit 900 seconds. | Test with a controlled blocking fake and define cancellation behavior; measure return time before promising a 90-second bound. |
| Key validation/display limitations | `api_client.py:validate_key` accepts some “unavailable” errors. `config.py:display` exposes the nested key map; UI key prompts are visible. | Add isolated cases distinguishing auth success from service failure, and check masking across all displayed key fields. Never use real keys in fixtures. |
| Fresh setup and packaging need validation | Manual-install config starts with an empty model; installer supplies a historical model name. Installer fallback launcher assumes a relative checkout location. Package Python-floor support is unverified. | In a disposable full checkout, check manual and editable startup on supported Python/Termux versions and explicit model selection. Document actual results rather than assuming the defaults work. |

A smaller parser edge case is also visible: `CommandSystem.parse_command("/")` indexes an empty split result; unknown nonempty slash commands are sent to `/ask`. Confirm the intended handling with a focused regression before changing dispatch behavior.

## Verification and remaining setup gap

All seven supplied test modules were read. The REST tests mock HTTP; repair execution is mocked; watch tests actually touch the process user's home and start threads. There is no supplied main-loop or installer integration suite. Procedures for an authorized future development session are in [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md#testing); no passing test count, coverage result, latency result or device certification is asserted here.

The documentation was checked against file contents, then reviewed for cross-links and preservation of useful material. No Git revision, index status or effective ignore state was available through the permitted tools. The supplied `.gitignore` contains no apparent rule targeting these visible root Markdown files; that is not a Git tracking check.

[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#context-maintenance) contains the new maintenance rule and points here. The session supplied personal AGENTS-style guidance but did not establish that a new root file is automatically loaded by a particular client/version/settings. **Automatic loading remains unconfirmed**, and the final `Adopted` marker is deferred under the adoption skill's incomplete-setup rule. A future eligible client session must establish loading before recording adoption as complete. The skills are installed in this working environment but are excluded from the Markdown-only handoff; do not assume a recipient has them.

# Contributing to ARIA

Thank you for your interest in contributing to ARIA! This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing.

## Code of Conduct

- Be respectful and inclusive
- Focus on the code, not the person
- Help others learn and grow

## Getting Started

Returning contributors should read [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) first, then the affected sections of [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). The 2026-11-14 documentation review inspected source and tests only; it did not execute the project or establish passing tests.

### Prerequisites

- Package metadata declares Python 3.8+; the supported runtime floor has not been tested in this handoff
- Git
- Termux (for testing on actual device)

### Setup Development Environment

The commands below require a full source checkout, not the Markdown-only handoff. Use a disposable account/container or equivalent isolated home for testing: the watch suite accesses the process user's real `~/.aria` (details below). These are procedures for an authorized development session, not commands executed during this documentation task.

```bash
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/Alex72-py/aria-termux.git
cd aria-termux

# Create virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install in development mode
pip install -r requirements.txt
pip install -e .
pip install pytest pytest-cov

# Run tests
pytest tests/
```

## Development Workflow

### 1. Create a Feature Branch

```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
```

### 2. Make Changes

- Follow PEP 8 style guide
- Add docstrings to functions
- Add type hints where possible
- Keep functions focused and testable

### 3. Write Tests

- Add tests for new functionality
- Run tests: `pytest tests/`
- Aim for >80% code coverage

### 4. Commit Changes

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "feat: Add your feature description"
```

### 5. Push and Create Pull Request

```bash
git push origin feature/your-feature-name
```

## Code Style

### Python Style Guide

- Follow PEP 8
- Use 4 spaces for indentation
- Maximum line length: 100 characters
- Use meaningful variable names

### Example

```python
def analyze_error(self, error_output: str) -> dict:
    """
    Analyze error and provide suggestions.
    
    Args:
        error_output: Error output from shell
        
    Returns:
        Analysis dictionary with suggestions
    """
    # Implementation here
    pass
```

## Testing

### Running Tests

`tests/test_watch_mode.py` creates `~/.aria`, starts polling threads, writes `last_fail.json` and `watch.log`, and deletes those two files in teardown. Enabling the watcher can also create `runtime_errors.log` and `watch_targets.json`. Do not point this suite at valuable existing ARIA state. Config tests use temporary paths; repair execution and REST API cases use mocks.

The inspected inventory has seven test modules. The existing >80% coverage goal is an aspiration, not a measured result. No supplied integration test covers the main REPL or installer, and unit mocks do not establish live provider or device compatibility. See [coverage map](ARCHITECTURE.md#testing-architecture).

```bash
# Run all tests
pytest tests/

# Run specific test file
pytest tests/test_api_client.py

# Run with coverage
pytest --cov=aria tests/
```

### Writing Tests

```python
def test_feature_name():
    """Test description."""
    # Setup
    obj = MyClass()
    
    # Execute
    result = obj.method()
    
    # Assert
    assert result == expected_value
```

## Documentation

- Update README.md for user-facing changes
- Add docstrings to all public functions
- Include examples in docstrings
- Update CHANGELOG.md for significant changes
- Update [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) when project state, decisions, blockers or next actions change; keep historical claims in the changelog distinct from current implementation. See [context maintenance](AGENTS.md#context-maintenance).

## Commit Message Format

```
<type>: <subject>

<body>

<footer>
```

### Types

- `feat`: New feature
- `fix`: Bug fix
- `docs`: Documentation
- `style`: Code style (no logic change)
- `refactor`: Code refactoring
- `test`: Adding tests
- `chore`: Build, dependencies, etc.

### Example

```
feat: Add watch mode for auto-error detection

Implement real-time shell monitoring that detects errors
and suggests fixes from knowledge base.

Closes #123
```

## Pull Request Process

1. Update README.md with any new features
2. Update version number in setup.py
3. Ensure all tests pass
4. Request review from maintainers
5. Address feedback and re-request review
6. Merge after approval

## Reporting Bugs

### Bug Report Template

```markdown
**Describe the bug**
A clear description of what the bug is.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Run command...
2. See error...

**Expected behavior**
What should happen instead.

**Environment**
- OS: [e.g. Termux, Ubuntu]
- Python version: [e.g. 3.8, 3.11]
- ARIA version: [e.g. 1.0.0]
- Provider and model: [e.g. openrouter, <model name>]

**Additional context**
Any other relevant information.
```

## Feature Requests

### Feature Request Template

```markdown
**Is your feature request related to a problem?**
Describe the problem.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Clear description of the desired feature.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Other solutions or features you've considered.

**Additional context**
Any other relevant information.
```

## Project Structure

```
aria-termux/
├── aria/                  # Main package
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── main.py            # Main loop, command dispatch, setup wizard
│   ├── api_client.py      # Provider abstraction (Google, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM)
│   ├── command_system.py  # Slash command registry and parsing
│   ├── config.py          # JSON config (~/.aria/config.json)
│   ├── guardian.py        # Risk scoring and confirmation prompts
│   ├── knowledge_base.py  # Offline Termux troubleshooting data
│   ├── repair_agent.py    # Local-first fix planning
│   ├── watch_mode.py      # Cross-session error capture
│   ├── ui.py              # Terminal UI components
│   └── utils.py           # Utilities
├── tests/                 # Test suite
├── install.sh             # Installer
├── run_aria.py            # Run without installing
├── setup.py               # Package setup
├── ARCHITECTURE.md        # Design overview
├── CHANGELOG.md           # Notable changes
├── README.md              # User documentation
├── CONTRIBUTING.md        # This file
└── LICENSE                # MIT License
```

## Areas for Contribution

- **Knowledge Base**: Add more Termux error patterns and solutions
- **Commands**: Implement new slash commands
- **UI**: Improve terminal UI and animations
- **Performance**: Optimize API calls and response times
- **Documentation**: Improve guides and examples
- **Testing**: Increase test coverage
- **Platforms**: Test and fix issues on different Android versions

## Questions?

- Check [existing issues](https://github.com/Alex72-py/aria-termux/issues)
- Open a new issue if yours isn't covered
- Review ARCHITECTURE.md and the code comments

## License

By contributing, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the MIT License.

README.md.text:
# ARIA — AI Terminal Co-Pilot for Termux [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-89%25-3776ab?logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://python.org) [![Shell](https://img.shields.io/badge/Shell-11%25-4EAA25?logo=gnu-bash&logoColor=white)](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) **A terminal AI assistant that actually understands Termux.**
--- ## Returning to the project? Start with [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) for the source-reviewed state, reading order and unresolved issues. [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) describes current implementation; [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) preserves release history. This handoff was reviewed statically on 2026-11-14; no tests, installs or live provider checks were run. ## Status ARIA was originally built for the Google Gemma 4 Challenge ([write-up](https://dev.to/alex72py/i-built-aria-an-ai-terminal-co-pilot-for-termux-using-gemma-4-be4)). That's over, and it's now a regular open-source tool that works with any model its providers offer. It's built and maintained by one person, so work is driven by [issues](https://github.com/Alex72-py/aria-termux/issues) and pull requests rather than a deadline. - **Maintainer-described stable features:** the core loop, slash commands, Guardian, watch mode, offline knowledge base, and three providers (Google AI Studio, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM). This is the existing project status, not a runtime certification from the documentation review; see [known implementation gaps](CONTEXT.md#open-issues-and-proposed-next-actions). --- ## What is this? ARIA is an AI assistant that lives in your terminal. It knows about Termux, Android filesystem quirks, proot containers, clang-not-gcc, and all the weird stuff you deal with when developing on a phone. It can answer questions, diagnose errors, suggest fixes, and auto-repair broken installs, all from a slash-command interface inside Termux. **It's lightweight.** One dependency (`rich`). Everything else is stdlib. No bloated frameworks. --- ## Screenshots
Click to expand ### Startup ### Model Selection ### Error Analysis
## Demo https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1795a534-37a9-4f81-b217-e13b95cb1836 --- ## Install ```bash pkg update && pkg upgrade -y pkg install python git -y git clone https://github.com/Alex72-py/aria-termux.git cd aria-termux pip install -r requirements.txt --break-system-packages python run_aria.py ``` The Google provider works with no extra packages. If `google-generativeai` is installed, ARIA uses it. If not, ARIA talks to the Google API directly over HTTPS. You only need the package if you specifically want the SDK path: ```bash pip install google-generativeai --break-system-packages ``` --- ## First Run ARIA opens the setup wizard when provider, model or API key is missing. The wizard asks for these values, Guardian mode and auto-apply. Example choices (prompt wording depends on saved values): ``` Choose provider [google/openrouter/nvidia_nim]: google Enter API key: Enter model: Enable Guardian mode? [y/n]: y Enable auto-apply for fixes? [y/n]: n ``` The wizard saves configuration and attempts a provider key check. Failure produces a warning; it does not necessarily stop startup. Key input is ordinary visible console input. A fresh manual install has an empty model default, so enter a model explicitly; the installer seeds a model name whose live availability is unverified. **Get a free key:** - Google: [aistudio.google.com/app/apikey](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey) - OpenRouter: [openrouter.ai/keys](https://openrouter.ai/keys) - NVIDIA NIM: [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com) --- ## Usage Just type. Bare text goes to the model as a question. Or use slash commands: | Command | What it does | |---------|-------------| | `/ask ` | Ask anything | | `/fix` | Diagnose the last failed command | | `/fix "error text"` | Diagnose a specific error | | `/install ` | Plan an installation; execute after confirmation or when auto-apply is enabled | | `/provider list` | Show configured providers | | `/provider openrouter` | Switch provider | | `/provider cycle` | Rotate to next provider | | `/provider key ` | Update a provider's API key | | `/model list` | List available models | | `/model set ` | Switch model | | `/kb ` | Search offline knowledge base | | `/watch` | Toggle watch mode (monitors configured hook/log sources) | | `/watch status` | List registered watch targets | | `/watch add pid= log= name=` | Register a PID and/or log target; values cannot contain spaces | | `/watch remove ` | Remove a registered target | | `/status` | Show current state | | `/config` | Re-run the setup wizard | | `/history` | Show recent in-memory command history | | `/help` | Show all commands | | `/exit` or `/quit` | Leave the REPL | These are interactive commands, not shell subcommands such as `aria ask`. Unknown slash commands fall through to the model like bare text. ### Watch Mode The manual install above does not install a shell hook. The optional `install.sh` installs dependencies/package and hooks, edits `.bashrc`/`.zshrc` and PATH, removes old ARIA hook blocks, and creates or adjusts config. Review those changes before using the installer in a full checkout, then reload the relevant shell startup file. With a hook installed, enable `/watch` and work in another session. The hook writes the latest failure to `~/.aria/last_fail.json`; `/fix` reads and clears it. The current Zsh hook omits the timestamp required for automatic watch detection, although manual `/fix` can still read it. Watch polls about once per second and displays queued notifications before the next input prompt. Without hooks, direct command output to `~/.aria/watch.log`, or supply error text to `/fix`. See [error detection flow](ARCHITECTURE.md#error-detection--fix-flow) for target logs, event fields and notification limits. --- ## Providers | Provider | Endpoint | Auth | |----------|----------|------| | `google` | Google AI Studio | API key from aistudio | | `openrouter` | openrouter.ai | API key from dashboard | | `nvidia_nim` | integrate.api.nvidia.com | API key from build.nvidia.com | ARIA auto-discovers available models from whichever provider you're using. Run `/model list` to see them and `/model set ` to switch. --- ## Architecture ``` aria/ ├── main.py — Main loop, command dispatch, setup wizard ├── api_client.py — Provider abstraction (Google, OpenRouter, NVIDIA) ├── command_system.py — Slash command registry and parsing ├── config.py — JSON config management (~/.aria/config.json) ├── guardian.py — Risk scoring and confirmation prompts ├── knowledge_base.py — Offline Termux troubleshooting data ├── watch_mode.py — File watcher for cross-session error capture ├── repair_agent.py — Local-first fix planning (no model call needed) └── ui.py — Rich terminal output, spinners, formatting ``` The REST paths use Python's `urllib`; Google uses its SDK when installed and REST otherwise. OpenRouter and NVIDIA share an OpenAI-compatible implementation. Provider switching rebuilds the client and discovers models. For the full design, see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). --- ## Guardian Guardian classifies commands with regex patterns and returns a risk level plus a confirmation flag. It does not itself prompt or gate every execution path. | Level | Score | Confirmation flag | |-------|-------|-------------------| | Low | 0 | No | | Medium | 40 | Yes | | High | 70 | Yes | | Critical | 100 | Yes | Local `/fix` auto-repair uses that flag and installation-command prefixes to filter execution. `/install` uses a separate plan-level confirmation unless auto-apply is enabled. Safe-pattern matching runs first and can miss dangerous combinations; treat the result as advisory. See [execution boundaries](ARCHITECTURE.md#guardian-safety-layer). Auto-apply defaults to false. The current `/fix` response suggests `/fix --apply`, but the handler does not parse that flag; it is treated as error text and does not enable execution. --- ## Config Stored at `~/.aria/config.json`: ```json { "provider": "google", "api_key": "your-active-key", "api_keys": { "google": "...", "openrouter": "...", "nvidia_nim": "..." }, "model": "your-model-name", "temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 8192, "guardian_mode": true, "watch_mode": false, "auto_apply": false } ``` Configuration supports these environment variables: ```bash export ARIA_API_KEY="..." export ARIA_PROVIDER="openrouter" export ARIA_MODEL="your-model-name" ``` Provider-specific variables `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, and `NVIDIA_NIM_API_KEY` are also supported. Saved provider keys can supersede `ARIA_API_KEY` during startup; see [load order](ARCHITECTURE.md#configuration-schema). Keys are stored in plain JSON. `/config` and `/provider key` save changes but do not fully synchronize the active client; restarting reloads config (subject to environment overrides). --- ## Dependencies | Package | Why | Required | |---------|-----|:--------:| | `rich` | Terminal UI, syntax highlighting, spinners | Yes | | `google-generativeai` | Optional SDK for the Google provider (ARIA falls back to plain HTTPS without it) | No | Everything else (HTTP, JSON, threading, config) is stdlib. All three providers work with no extra packages. --- ## Testing Use a disposable test environment: the watch tests write and delete files in the process user's `~/.aria`. With test dependencies installed, the documented commands are: ```bash pytest -q pytest -v # verbose ``` These were not run for this handoff. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#testing) for setup and coverage limits. --- ## Known limitations - Watch mode uses file polling and prompt-boundary notifications; see the hook and context-routing gaps above. - AI features need internet. Knowledge-base lookup needs no network, but the REPL still requires nonempty provider/model/key configuration to finish setup. - Built for Termux on Android. It runs on Linux too, but that's not the focus. - Auto-fix suggestions should be reviewed before applying. --- ## Contributing Issues and PRs are welcome. answers.answer: Guardian checks safe regex patterns first with unanchored re.search; any safe match immediately returns LOW. Otherwise, it selects the highest matching dangerous level; no match also yields LOW. Scores are fixed, not additive: LOW 0 (no confirmation), MEDIUM 40, HIGH 70, CRITICAL 100 (confirmation flag true for all three). Guardian returns advisory flags rather than prompting or protecting every execution path. Setting guardian_mode=false does not disable it inside the app: Guardian is constructed enabled, and setup never disables it for a false saved preference.

ARIA_PROVIDER supplies the provider, ARIA_MODEL the model, and ARIA_API_KEY the general key. Provider-specific keys come from GOOGLE_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY and NVIDIA_NIM_API_KEY. Configuration loads saved values/defaults, migration/backfill, general ARIA_* overrides, then provider-specific keys. Provider-specific environment keys populate api_keys and replace the active key when the provider matches. Startup prefers api_keys[provider] over the general api_key, so a saved key for the selected provider can supersede ARIA_API_KEY; a matching provider-specific environment key takes precedence over that saved provider key.

Partially established: APIClient makes at most three generation attempts by default, stopping on success or a nonretryable error. Retryable failures wait 1 second and then 2 seconds between attempts. Exhaustion returns error/help text suggesting /kb and provider/config commands, not offline model inference. Google REST can retry a rejected separate system instruction with that instruction folded into the prompt, so one outer attempt can involve multiple HTTP requests. However, the documents do not enumerate which REST HTTP errors, transport failures or response errors are retryable versus immediately terminal; that part cannot be established.

No: --apply is not parsed as an execution flag; /fix treats it as error text. Execution depends on saved auto_apply, which defaults to false. With auto_apply enabled, local repair steps are filtered by auto_run, Guardian's confirmation flag and allowed installation-command prefixes. At most four steps run, stopping on a nonzero result. Model-assisted suggestions are displayed rather than automatically executed. Thus typing the hint does not itself authorize or apply the previously displayed plan.

The optional install.sh installs the hooks, edits .bashrc/.zshrc and PATH, removes old ARIA hook blocks, and creates or adjusts configuration; reload the relevant shell startup file afterward. Following the README Install steps does not install a hook. Bash and Zsh differ for watch mode: Bash writes cmd, code, cwd and ts; Zsh omits ts. The watcher requires a new nonempty timestamp, so the Zsh hook does not support automatic detection as written. Manual /fix can still read its JSON because it has no timestamp requirement. Neither hook captures stderr.

Partially established: the documents report Python >=3.8 and rich>=13.0.0 as the sole required dependency; google-generativeai is optional. The installed console command is aria, pointing to aria.main:main and opening the interactive REPL. There is no aria/cli.py or Click dependency, and no implemented aria ask / aria fix shell-subcommand interface; use /ask and /fix inside the REPL. The package metadata's distribution name and a complete optional-dependency declaration are not retained in the documents, so those cannot be established from the repository directory name or installation examples.

The current architecture explicitly says scores are not additive; CONTEXT identifies earlier additive-score claims as conflicting with inspected code or lacking evidence. Safe substrings masking dangerous commands are recorded as an unresolved issue, with a proposal to agree a consistent policy before changing code. That does not establish whether the behavior was intended.

Its Watch Mode section now describes install.sh as optional and explains its shell/configuration changes, while explicitly saying the manual steps do not install hooks. This documents an available installation mechanism, but does not establish the maintainer's supported or preferred path.
